SEARCH
Package com.privatechain.core.spi

Interface BlockchainStorage

All Known Implementing Classes:
FileSystemStorage, InMemoryStorage, LevelDBStorage, RocksDBStorage
public interface BlockchainStorage
Service Provider Interface (SPI) for persistent block storage.

Implementations must be thread-safe for concurrent reads; writes must be serialized (NFR-REL-01, FR-STOR-06). The library ships four built-in implementations in the blockchain-storage module:

  • InMemoryStorage — HashMap-backed, for testing (FR-STOR-02)
  • LevelDBStorage — crash-safe persistent storage (FR-STOR-03)
  • RocksDBStorage — high write-throughput persistent storage (FR-STOR-04)
  • FileSystemStorage — one JSON file per block, zero native deps (FR-STOR-05)

Contract

  • Blocks are stored by their integer index (unique per chain).
  • saveBlock(Block) is idempotent: saving the same block twice must not throw; the second call is a no-op or an overwrite of identical data.
  • loadAll() must return blocks in ascending index order.
Since:
1.0.0

  • Method Details

    • saveBlock

      void saveBlock(Block block)
      Persists a block to the underlying storage medium.

      Must be atomic: either the block is fully written or the storage state is unchanged (no partial writes). Implementations backed by LevelDB or RocksDB satisfy this by writing inside an atomic batch.

      Parameters:
      block - the block to persist (non-null)
      Throws:
      BlockValidationException - if the write fails

    • loadBlock

      Returns:

      Throws:

    • loadAll

      List<Block> loadAll()
      Returns all stored blocks in ascending index order.

      For large chains callers should prefer iterating via index ranges rather than loading the full chain into memory at once.

      Returns:
      non-null, possibly empty, ordered list of all blocks

      void deleteAll()
